newsitem.title: ITALY: Lira up at highest levels vs mark for over 2 years.
newsitem.headline: Lira up at highest levels vs mark for over 2 years.

text.p: The lira firmed past a resistance level of 985 lire per mark in late European trade and ventured into territory not seen since the start of July 1994.
Dealers said the lira, which rejoined Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM) last weekend, was helped by the stronger dollar and might reach 980 per mark near term.
"While the tone is positive in other markets there is no reason to sell lire," one dealer said, noting that bond markets were also strong.

The lira was quoted at 985.42/5.77 per mark by 1555 GMT. It has strengthened steadily since Sunday when EU finance ministers reinstated it in the ERM after two years' absence, assigning it a central parity of 990 per mark.
The December Btp futures contract on LIFFE rose to a record peak at 128.84 earlier on Friday, outstripping the high of 128.70 set on November 25.
